• Article 324 – Election Commission.
• Part XV deals with elections.
• Multi-member body since 1989.
• CEC removal is similar to that of a Supreme Court judge.
• Expenses charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
• Does NOT conduct local elections.
CEC removal is similar to that of a Supreme Court judge.

items: The Election Commission does NOT conduct local body elections (Panchayats and Municipalities).
Removal of the CEC requires the same procedure as a Supreme Court judge.
Election Commission expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 324 provides for the establishment of the Election Commission.
Part XV of the Indian Constitution deals exclusively with elections.
The Election Commission became a multi-member body in the year 1989.
The removal process of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is similar to that of a Supreme Court judge.
All administrative expenses of the Election Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
The Election Commission does NOT conduct local (Panchayat and Municipality) elections.
